name: UD -> SOP rules v1.4 against v1.3 on a fresh held-out sample (EN, RO, mixed; test, OOD, wild), with a separately labelled host-normalized score (synonym and frame list, owner answer to Q-SYM-2)
registered_by: symbolic-rules-agent (owner answers to Q-SYM-1..3 of 2026-09-29, relayed by the orchestrator)

owner_requests.Q-SYM-1: "nu eliminam cazuri valide doar ca sa treaca verificarile, sa ramina clar, ce pica, pica; o sa incercam sa fixam din fine tuning": strict scoring stays exactly as it is; no evaluation normalization hides relation/object boundary misses; a tolerant host-linking score may be reported only beside strict and labelled as such.
owner_requests.Q-SYM-2: "ti-am zis sa avem o lista de sinonime, sa joace rolul hostului cum zici tu, din rezultatele pe care le scoate le putem normaliza. analizeaza daca e suficient o lista mare de sinonime": build a large synonym and frame list that normalizes produced outputs as host work, measure what it resolves on data not used to build it, and report strict and host-normalized scores side by side.
owner_requests.rules: Fix what is clearly fixable (proposals.md R1-R19 and tree repairs); build v1.4 from training/dev data only; measure on a fresh held-out sample drawn before any rule change; paired bootstrap CIs vs v1.3 including wild, EN and RO rows. CPU only (Stanza on CPU); no training.

kind: evaluation-only (CPU inference; no training, no LLM calls)
frozen_before_results: Written right after the fresh sample was drawn (eval/reports/current/ud-rules-v14/sample.json, 2026-09-29T17:22:21Z, sha256 5a7bb2033137b72493fb4d0899a267aba032d726ccb291d81d9e42300ddbd62a) while lib/ud-to-sop was still byte-identical to frozen-rules-v1.3 (SHA256SUMS verified). The v1.3 predictions of the sample are generated before any rule change and are not scored or inspected until v1.4 is frozen.

systems.parser: Stanza 1.10.1 (EN default package, RO RRT) through training/python/ud_parse_worker.py on the CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty); input = each rules version's own maskMessage(question)
systems.a: ud-rules-v1.3 (eval/reports/current/baseline-ud-rules/frozen-rules-v1.3/, loaded from the frozen copy)
systems.b: ud-rules-v1.4: lib/ud-to-sop after rule changes developed on datasets/formalizer-v1 train/dev rows and on the example sentences written in proposals.md only; frozen under eval/reports/current/baseline-ud-rules/frozen-rules-v1.4/ (SHA256SUMS) before any v1.4 conversion of a sample row
systems.host_normalization: sop/frames.mjs with the frame and synonym list config/dictionary/frames.tsv (built by tools/frames.mjs from datasets/formalizer-v1 train/dev rows, the train verification world, the host dictionary and Princeton WordNet 3.0 verb synsets); frozen (digest recorded) before any sample row is normalized

sample.size: 600 messages: 240 sealed formalizer-v1 test, 180 formalizer-ood-v1, 180 formalizer-wild-v1; every language (283 en, 272 ro, 45 mixed)
sample.eligibility: every row except the 400 consumed rows of eval-symbolic-layers-en-v1 and every surface variant of their semantic cases; one row per semantic_case_id
sample.strata: source x language x question-type group x length (as in eval-symbolic-layers-en-v1), proportional largest-remainder allocation with at least one row per non-empty stratum
sample.stages: nested stratified stages of 150 and 300 rows (seed 42) and the full 600

metrics.strict: unchanged harness: test/OOD execution_equivalent_tolerant of eval/run.mjs (row world); wild: D1-tolerant all-proposition F1 = 1 against any accepted gold (tools/research/ud-baseline-eval.mjs tolerantScores). Owner decision Q-SYM-1: this is the headline score.
metrics.host_normalized: the same scorer after the host frame normalization rewrites the prediction (relation synonym to a listed frame, relation+preposition frame to role name, single-oblique role relabel, relation/object boundary shift); for the wild suite the gold is normalized too. Always reported beside strict, never instead of it.
metrics.secondary: mean D1-tolerant all-proposition F1; admitted (valid) output rate; the normalization gain (normalized - strict) per rules version

outcomes.primary: paired difference of strict match, v1.4 - v1.3, paired cluster bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 7; clusters = semantic cases), overall
outcomes.reported_slices: test, OOD, wild; en, ro, mixed; wild-en, wild-ro, wild-mixed; the same for the host-normalized score and for the normalization gain
outcomes.q_sym_2: on the 146 Layer-2 misses of eval-symbolic-layers-en-v1 under v1.3 (sealed rows never used to build the list): how many of the 38 C_role, the 30 C_boundary and all 146 become matches after host normalization; and the normalization gain on the fresh sample

hypotheses.H1: v1.4 raises the strict match rate over v1.3 on the fresh sample (95% CI excludes 0).
hypotheses.H2: No source or language slice gets worse: no slice has a 95% CI entirely below 0.
hypotheses.H3: A synonym and frame list is not sufficient alone: host normalization resolves at least half of the 38 C_role misses but less than half of all 146 Layer-2 misses (the rest are rules and question-form differences a list cannot express).

stop_rules: Broken condition: at stage 150, more than 20% of v1.4 outputs are empty or not admitted -> stop, fix as a recorded deviation, restart on the same sample.
Harm: at stage 150 or 300, the 95% CI of the overall strict delta lies entirely below 0 -> stop and report v1.4 as a regression.

Success is not a reason to stop early: the owner asked for CIs on wild, EN and RO slices, and a full CPU run costs minutes, so the full 600 rows are scored unless a stop rule above fires. Every stage result is written (compare-150.json, compare-300.json, compare-full.json) and recorded.
rigor: v1.4 and the frame list are developed on datasets/formalizer-v1 train/dev rows only; no sealed row (fresh sample or otherwise) is converted with a development version.
The v1.3 and v1.4 predictions and the frame list are frozen (SHA-256) before the first compare run.
Strict scoring is the unchanged harness; the normalized score is labelled and reported beside it.
No training; GPU untouched (Stanza on CPU); port 9999 untouched; only this experiment's processes are stopped.

deviations.what: Host dictionary change during development (sop/dictionary.mjs compile-3): a Romanian relation form with an inflected copula also answers to its fi lemma form ("e antrenorul de la" -> "fi antrenorul de la"), and a Romanian verb chain in the short infinitive is translated with an English to-infinitive ("vrea învăța" -> "want to learn"). The strict harness links through this dictionary.
deviations.why: DS014 prescribes these lemma forms for Romanian output; the dictionary did not link them, so any DS014-conform producer lost Romanian rows. Owner authorization: synonym entries and host fixes that are clearly fixable.
deviations.effect: Applies to v1.3 and v1.4 alike: both are scored at compare time with the same frozen host data (eval/reports/current/ud-rules-v14/host-data.SHA256SUMS). On the development slice it moved v1.3 from 29.7% to 30.7%.

deviations.what: The formalizer-wild-v1 suite was re-adjudicated on 10 rows (owner answer to Q-SYM-3; eval/reports/current/ud-rules-v14/gold-readjudication.jsonl); its sha256 changed from 077e7164… (recorded in sample.json) to 548d76be….
deviations.effect: None of the 10 rows is in this sample (they belong to the consumed eval-symbolic-layers-en-v1 sample); every sample row is byte-identical, so no score of this experiment changes.

deviations.what: training/python/ud_parse_worker.py was changed by another agent at 19:21 (optional forced language for SymbolicLM; default behaviour unchanged) before the v1.3 predictions were generated; frozen-rules-v1.4 records the current worker hash.
deviations.effect: Both rule versions parse through the same worker without the new option, so the paired comparison is unaffected.

deviations.what: Post hoc bug fix of the host normalizer (sop/frames.mjs boundary split): a relation that names no frame was split before a participle or after a bare copula ("be based in" -> "be" + "based in", then "be" read as a synonym of another frame), which turned 2 strict matches of the sample into normalized misses. The split now moves only a noun tail and never splits off "be/fi/have/avea/do/get". Found while reading the full-sample normalization losses.
deviations.why: A correctness bug of the host step, not a tuning choice; the strict score (primary) does not use the normalizer.
deviations.effect: Strict numbers unchanged. Host-normalized, full sample: v1.3 28.2% -> 28.5%, v1.4 32.7% -> 33.0%; normalization losses 2 -> 0. The pre-fix results are kept (compare-*.normalizer-before-D4.json); the fix is post hoc and labelled so.
